Series::detach¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::detach() const -> Series

What It Does¶

detach() returns a new Series value with the same visible data but without the current reverse-mode tracking lineage.

This is the read-side, non-mutating form of detaching.

Use it when you want:

  • the current numeric values

  • no current reverse-mode connection back through how those values were produced

That is the real contract. The important promise is about reverse-mode state, not about forcing one specific storage strategy.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series A detached Series value.

On the current verified public surface, the detached result starts untracked.

Reverse-Mode Meaning¶

Detaching creates a new autograd boundary.

Before detaching, later reverse-mode can treat the current value as depending on earlier tracked sources.

After detaching, later reverse-mode treats the detached value as a fresh value with no public reverse-mode path back through the pre-detach computation.

In mathematical terms, if an earlier tracked source x produced some intermediate value and you then call detach(), later objectives built from the detached result are no longer differentiated with respect to that earlier path.

Examples¶

Example 1. detach() preserves the visible values.

auto base = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
auto detached = base.detach();

std::cout << "base=" << base << "\n";
std::cout << "detached=" << detached << "\n";

Output¶

base=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3]
detached=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3]

Example 2. On the current verified surface, later in-place mutation of the detached result does not rewrite the original series in this example.

auto base = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
auto detached = base.detach();
detached.add_(10.0);

std::cout << "base=" << base << "\n";
std::cout << "detached=" << detached << "\n";

Output¶

base=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3]
detached=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[11, 12, 13]

This is worth documenting carefully: the public contract you should rely on is the detach of reverse-mode state. Storage-sharing details are not the point of the method.

Example 3. Reverse-mode built from the detached result no longer populates sensitivity on the original tracked source.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, pluss::cfg::tracks_slope());

auto y = x.detach().mul(3.0);
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "x_has_dL_dx=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

The scalar objective is

L = sum(3 * detach(x))

Numerically, the detached value contains the same entries as x, but for reverse-mode purposes it is now a fresh boundary. So this objective is not propagated back through the original tracked x.

Output¶

x_has_dL_dx=false

Example 4. The detached result starts with tracking disabled even if the original source was tracked.

auto source = pluss::make_series({4.0, 5.0});
source.tracks_slope_(true);
auto detached = source.detach();

std::cout << "source_tracks=" << (source.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "detached_tracks=" << (detached.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

source_tracks=true
detached_tracks=false

Example 5. A detached result can become a new tracked leaf if you enable tracking on the detached value itself.

auto source = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, pluss::cfg::tracks_slope());
auto detached = source.detach();
detached.tracks_slope_(true);

detached.mul(3.0).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "source_has_dL_dsource=" << (source.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "detached_dL_ddetached=" << detached.sensitivity() << "\n";

The new scalar objective is differentiated with respect to the detached leaf, not with respect to the original source:

L = 3d1 + 3d2 + 3d3

so the detached leaf stores [3, 3, 3], while the original source remains outside the new reverse path.

Output¶

source_has_dL_dsource=false
detached_dL_ddetached=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[3, 3, 3]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • detach() is about severing reverse-mode lineage, not about changing the values.

  • The detached result starts untracked.

  • If you want to detach the current handle in place instead of creating a new value, use detach_.

  • If you later re-enable tracking on the detached result, it becomes a new leaf with a new reverse history, not a continuation of the old one.

Summary¶

Use detach() when you want the current numeric value as a fresh autograd boundary: same visible data, no current upstream reverse-mode connection.

See Also¶

  • Series::detach_: in-place detach on the current handle.

  • Series::tracks_slope_: turn the detached result into a new tracked leaf if needed.

  • Series::reverse: the downstream reverse entrypoint that detached values stop feeding into upstream history.
